He was considered one of the top freshman in 2013–14 and is tipped to be a high draft pick in [[2014 NBA draft|2014]].[http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2014/01/syracuses_tyler_ennis_dukes_jabari_parker_have_been_top_freshmen_in_the_nation.html Duke's Jabari Parker, Syracuse's Tyler Ennis have been top freshmen in the nation][http://college-basketball.si.com/2014/01/17/freshman-tyler-ennis-syracuse-orange-jim-boeheim-pittsburgh/ Arguably nation’s most valuable freshman, Tyler Ennis leads No. 2 Syracuse][http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10365588/2014-nba-draft-tyler-ennis-vaults-top-10-nik-stauskas-debuts-no-14 2014 NBA draft Big Board 6.0] ==High school career== Ennis first year playing high school basketball was played at [[Father Henry Carr Catholic Secondary School]] in [[Rexdale, Ontario]]. Ennis also attended [[Saint Benedict's Preparatory School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]]. In his junior year in 2011–12, Ennis led St. Benedict’s, coached by Mark Taylor, to a school-record 35 victories and the No. 2 ranking in New Jersey. He was named the Gatorade New Jersey Player of the Year while averaging 14.6 points and 7.1 assists per game. In his senior year in 2012–13, the Gray Bees finished with a record of 31-2 as Ennis was honored as the Star-Ledger Prep Player of the Year and earned All-Prep First Team recognition after averaging 20 points, 6.1 assists, 5.2 rebounds and 3.1 steals per game.{{cite web|title=Tyler Ennis - 2013-14 Men's Basketball|url=http://cuse.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=10335|work=Cuse.com|accessdate=May 15, 2014}} ==College career== In his freshman season at [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] in 2013–14, Ennis was named to the 2014 All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] second team, All-ACC Freshmen Team, and All-ACC Defensive Team. In 34 games, he averaged 12.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 2.1 steals in 35.7 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Tyler Ennis Stats|url=http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/tyler-ennis-1.html|work=Sports-Reference.com|accessdate=May 15, 2014}} On February 28, 2014, Ennis was named one of the 10 semi-finalists for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Top 10 National Semifinalists Named for 2014 Men's Naismith Trophy presented by AT&T |url=http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx|work=NaismithAwards.com|accessdate=February 28, 2014|date=February 28, 2014}} Ennis helped lead the Syracuse Orange past Western Michigan in the second round of the 2014 NCAA Tournament,{{cite web|title=March Madness: Canadian Tyler Ennis leads Syracuse in win|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/march-madness-canadian-tyler-ennis-leads-syracuse-in-win-1.2579898|work=CBC.ca|accessdate=March 22, 2014|date=March 20, 2014}} but missed a three-pointer at the buzzer of the following game that would have taken Syracuse past Dayton and into the Sweet Sixteen. ==International career== Ennis played for the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian men's national basketball team]] in the 2012 [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]], winning a bronze medal, and in the [[2013 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]], leading the tournament in scoring.[http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/07/syracuse_point_guard_tyler_enn_1.html Syracuse point guard Tyler Ennis led FIBA U19 championship in scoring] In the 2012 tournament, he was a teammate of fellow college standout, [[Andrew Wiggins]].{{cite web|title=2012 FIBA Americas U18 Championship For Men –
